title: Kerbside bins overview
text: City of Melbourne provides three kerbside bin services to houses: a food organics and garden organics (FOGO) bin with a lime-green lid, a co-mingled recycling bin, and a general waste (landfill) bin.

title: Collection frequency
text: For houses on the food and garden organics service, the 120-litre FOGO bin is collected weekly, the 120-litre general waste (landfill) bin is collected weekly, and the 240-litre co-mingled recycling bin is collected fortnightly.

title: What goes in the FOGO bin
text: The food organics and garden organics (FOGO) bin accepts all food scraps including meat, fruit and vegetable scraps, flowers, garden prunings, grass clippings, leaves, small branches, twigs and weeds. Collected organics are turned into mulch for Melbourne's parks and gardens.

title: Kitchen caddy and compostable liners
text: Households on the food organics service receive a kitchen caddy for collecting food scraps and 52 free compostable bin liners, supplied on an ongoing basis.

title: What goes in the recycling bin
text: The co-mingled recycling bin accepts aluminium cans, steel food cans, cardboard, glass bottles and jars, magazines, newspapers and office paper. Items must be placed in the recycling bin loose, not wrapped in a plastic bag. Metal lids are accepted; plastic lids are not.

title: Soft plastics and plastic bags
text: Soft plastics and plastic bags are not accepted in the kerbside recycling bin. Do not bag your recyclables, as bagged items cannot be sorted at the recycling facility.

title: Replacement and damaged bins
text: To request a replacement for a lost, stolen or damaged bin, contact the City of Melbourne on 9658 9658.

title: Free hard waste collection
text: City of Melbourne residents are entitled to one free hard waste collection per residential address each financial year, limited to one cubic metre of items. Commercial and retail addresses are not eligible.

title: Booking a hard waste collection
text: Hard waste collections must be booked online through the City of Melbourne hard waste booking portal. Collection dates are made available two months in advance. High-rise residents can ask their building manager to arrange a collection.

title: Accepted hard waste items
text: Hard waste collections accept household furniture, mattresses, white goods such as fridges, dishwashers and washing machines (with doors removed), and e-waste such as televisions, computers, printers and small appliances. E-waste must be separated and lithium batteries removed.

title: Placing hard waste out
text: Hard waste items must be placed on the kerbside or another accessible location on the day before the booked collection. Collectors will not enter private property.

title: Pet registration requirement
text: All cats and dogs over three months old living in the City of Melbourne must be registered with council. Dogs and cats must be microchipped before they can be registered.

title: Pet registration renewal and fees
text: Pet registration lasts one year and expires on 10 April each year. Pet registration fees have been waived for the 2026-27 registration period, so no fee is required.

title: How to register a pet
text: You can register a cat or dog online through City of Melbourne eServices or by completing the PDF application form. Existing registrations can be renewed online. Applications are processed within two business days. Contact animal.management@melbourne.vic.gov.au or 03 9658 9658.

title: Tradesperson parking permit
text: A tradesperson parking permit costs $108 per week (2025-26 fees) and is approved for a maximum of 13 weeks, with an extension option of 10 weeks. Tradespeople must park near the work address and display the permit on the dashboard.

title: Applying for a parking permit
text: Parking permit applications should be submitted at least five working days before the permit is needed, with payment included. Contact City of Melbourne Permits and Approvals at permits@melbourne.vic.gov.au or 03 9658 9658.

title: Healthcare and medical parking permits
text: A medical practitioner parking permit costs $535 and a healthcare support worker parking permit costs $261 (2025-26 fees). Reserved street parking costs $200 per day for the first bay and $100 per day for each additional bay.

title: Contacting council
text: The City of Melbourne customer service phone number is 03 9658 9658.
